marks.gloss_en: אל תפסיעו פסיעה גסה -- דאמר מר: a long stride takes 1/500 of one's eyesight
the baraita: do not take long strides
והכניסו חמה לעיר -- כדרב יהודה אמר רב: leave and enter by 'ki tov'
Rav (via Rav Yehuda): a person should always leave with 'ki tov' and enter with 'ki tov'
איני? והאמר רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה: two scholars on the road without words of Torah deserve burning -- how then can Joseph forbid halakha on the road?

R' Ilai bar Berechya: two Torah scholars walking on the road with no words of Torah between them deserve burning, as it is said 'as they went on and talked, behold a chariot of fire' (II Kgs 2:11) -- the reason is that there was speech; without it, they deserve burning
לא קשיא: הא למיגרס, הא לעיוני -- rote review on the road is required; in-depth examination is what Joseph forbade
the stam: [R' Elazar's warning] is for in-depth examination
the baraita: and they interrupt [the series] for New Moons and for the festive days written in Megillat Taanit
let no one say 'I am a student, I am not fit to be a yachid'; rather all Torah scholars are yechidim
R' Meir: not everyone who wishes to make himself a yachid does so; a student does
R' Shimon ben Elazar: not everyone who wishes to make himself a yachid does so; a student does
one fasting over a trouble that passed, or over a sick man who recovered -- he fasts and completes [the fast]
one who forgot and ate and drank -- let him not show himself before the community, nor indulge himself in luxuries
R' Elazar: 'do not fall out on the way' (Gen 45:24) -- Joseph told his brothers: do not occupy yourselves with a matter of halakha, lest the way grow angry with you
R' Chiyya (via Rav Yehuda): one walking on the road should not eat more than [one eats in] years of famine
